evidence.detail: css_url and js_url use version querystrings (?v=<git_commit_hash>) enabling safe far-future caching, but no far-future Expires or max-age header is set for these routes
The /banner/banner.css route returns a dynamically-generated CSS response with no Cache-Control or Expires header set
The cached() decorator sets 'no-cache' Cache-Control for HTML pages — static assets are served by Flask default send_from_directory with no long-lived caching configured
No commits found setting far-future Expires or max-age headers for static assets; only session/DB expiry commits returned

triage.notes: Comments on the issue indicate this should be done in CloudFlare or nginx rather than Flask; banner.css is also a candidate since it is dynamically generated but infrequently changes. The decision of whether to fix in Flask (SEND_FILE_MAX_AGE_DEFAULT) vs CloudFlare cache rules is an infrastructure judgment call.
